summary:
The name of this Act is the "Alternative Development Finance Mobilization Act, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). Its main purpose is to mobilize alternative development finance through debentures, equity funds, and other financial or monetary instruments to arrange necessary resources for the overall economic prosperity and development of the country (Preamble, Page 1). This Act shall come into force on the thirty-first day from the date of certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Under this Act, the Nepal Government shall purchase 51 percent of the share capital of the Fund (Section 8, Subsection 4, Page 10). The Nepal Government and other institutions purchasing shares must pay the amount for the agreed shares in up to two installments within two fiscal years (Section 8, Subsection 5, Page 10). If any provincial government or local level wishes to purchase shares of the Fund, the shares may be sold based on the decision of the Nepal Government, Council of Ministers upon the recommendation of the Board of Directors (Section 8, Subsection 9, Page 11). The Nepal Government, Council of Ministers shall appoint the Chief Executive Officer of the Fund on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Chairman of the Public Service Commission (Section 19, Subsection 7, Page 25). Furthermore, the Nepal Government, Council of Ministers carries the responsibilities of approving the organizational structure of the Fund (Section 18, Subsection 1, Page 23), issuing necessary directions to the Fund (Section 54, Subsection 1, Page 50), and making rules for the implementation of this Act (Section 58, Page 50). The Fund must abide by the directions given by the Nepal Government (Section 54, Subsection 2, Page 50).

Under this Act, investment or financial assistance can be provided to national priority projects in sectors such as energy development, electricity transmission, roads, railways, airports, tunnels, special economic zones, urban infrastructure, irrigation, cable cars, and commercial agriculture (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 5; Section 4, Subsection 2, Page 6). However, investment shall not be made in projects with an estimated cost of less than Rs. 1 arab, projects with low estimated financial returns, projects unable to offer collateral, or projects implemented by a natural person (Section 5, Page 7). Before starting investment, a project must fulfill commitments regarding compliance with environmental standards, corporate governance, risk analysis, market study, and mechanisms for projection and evaluation of returns (Section 26, Subsection 1, Page 33). During project implementation, projects must undergo periodic evaluations of technical, commercial, climate, and environmental aspects, arrange risk mitigation, and coordinate with public-private sectors and local communities (Section 26, Subsection 2, Page 33). Institutions purchasing shares of the Fund must pay the share amount in up to two installments within two fiscal years (Section 8, Subsection 5, Page 10). If a project fails to comply with investment terms, misuses funds, provides false details, or fails to implement without reasonable cause, the Fund may recall the investment or withhold payment, and the project must immediately return the principal, interest, and service fees (Section 28, Subsection 1 and Subsection 2, Page 36). The annual general meeting of the shareholders of the Fund must be held within one year of the establishment of the Fund and thereafter within six months after the completion of each fiscal year (Section 48, Subsection 1, Page 48).

This Act establishes the "Alternative Development Finance Fund" as an autonomous corporate body headquartered in Kathmandu Valley to invest in projects (Section 6, Subsection 1 and Subsection 2, Page 7-8; Section 7, Subsection 1 and Subsection 2, Page 8). The authorized capital of the Fund shall be Rs. 1 kharab divided into 1 arab ordinary shares of Rs. 100 each, and the paid-up capital shall be Rs. 25 arab divided into 25 crore ordinary shares of Rs. 100 each, distributed as 51 percent to the Nepal Government, 25 percent to retirement funds or fund manager institutions, and 24 percent to insurance companies (Section 8, Subsection 1, Subsection 2 and Subsection 4, Page 8 and Page 10). The main functions of the Fund are to invest in infrastructure projects yielding high economic returns, issue debentures and financial instruments, mobilize foreign capital, provide guarantees, and offer advisory services (Section 9, Subsection 1, Page 10). To manage and operate the Fund, there shall be a Board of Directors chaired by the Secretary of the Ministry, comprising a Joint Secretary of the Ministry, an engineering service Joint Secretary from an infrastructure ministry, shareholder representatives, and two independent experts appointed by the Board (including at least one woman) for a two-year tenure (Section 10, Subsection 1 and Subsection 4, Page 13 and Page 15). To handle daily administration and management, the Nepal Government shall appoint a Chief Executive Officer recommended by a committee chaired by the Chairman of the Public Service Commission for a four-year term, who may be re-appointed for one additional term if performance is excellent (Section 19, Subsection 1, Subsection 3, Subsection 7 and Subsection 8, Page 24-25). The Chief Executive Officer must enter into an annual performance contract with the Board within thirty days of appointment (Section 23, Subsection 1, Page 29). The Fund shall contain proceeds from share sales, alternative finance mobilization, grants, interest, dividends, and service fees (Section 33, Subsection 1, Page 40). Additionally, the Fund must establish a general reserve fund by allocating at least 20 percent of net profit annually until it reaches double the paid-up capital, and 10 percent thereafter, alongside a free reserve fund (Section 35, Subsection 1 and Subsection 2, Page 42).
